fields.subnational_unit: Turkana County (arid and semi-arid land); Lodwar and sub-counties
fields.population: rural low-income households in Turkana County; national and county officials, NGO practitioners and community leaders (key informants)
fields.sample_size: cross-sectional household survey n = 475 (stratified random sampling across sub-counties); key informant interviews; six gender-stratified focus-group discussions; water-quality sampling; infrastructure assessments; hydrological scenario modelling of rainwater-harvesting systems
fields.effect_measure: three studies: (1) descriptive analysis of seasonal multiple water-source use (13 source types, 7 functional uses); (2) service-delivery, infrastructure-functionality and water-quality assessment; (3) scenario-based hydrological and cost modelling of nature-based rainwater-harvesting systems
fields.effect_estimate: Households use up to 13 water sources across 7 functional uses and switch seasonally, so single "main source" monitoring misstates access. Service delivery is unreliable and inequitable because of infrastructural deficiencies and fragmented governance (donor investment cycles, weak community oversight, devolved county arrangements). Microbial contamination is widespread in surface and informal sources; salinity and fluoride are elevated in many groundwater supplies. Subsurface dams offered storage up to 216,000 m3, strong multi-season reliability and USD 0.82-1.06 per m3, comparable to boreholes. No effect estimate on a legal or administrative exposure.
fields.model_type: descriptive household survey statistics, water-quality analysis, key informant and focus-group qualitative analysis, scenario hydrological modelling
fields.study_design: cross-sectional mixed-methods doctoral dissertation with three component studies (household survey, service-delivery and quality assessment, hydrological modelling)
fields.risk_of_bias_rating: MMAT (re-appraised 2026-10-04 on the full text; supersedes the abstract-only rating of 2026-09-28). S1=Yes (research questions per chapter); S2=Yes (survey, interviews and modelling address them). Mixed-methods criteria: 5.1(rationale)=Yes (complementary quantitative and qualitative components stated); 5.2(integration)=Can't tell (components are in separate chapters, linked by a resilience framework); 5.3(meta-inference)=Can't tell; 5.4(divergence)=Can't tell; 5.5(component quality)=No (fieldwork mainly in the wet season with dry-season conditions recalled retrospectively; recall bias and a single county acknowledged). Per MMAT's own guide, no composite score is computed.
fields.section: Full text (dissertation): Abstract; Chapter 1 (introduction, MWSU); Chapter 2 methods and service-delivery findings (partly)
fields.exact_location: Abstract pp ii-iii; Chapter 1 p1-30; data collection methods p131; governance and service-delivery findings in Chapter 2

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a PhD dissertation on rural water security in Turkana County, Kenya (household survey n = 475, key informant interviews, six focus groups, water-quality and hydrological modelling) read in full text 2026-10-04. Governance fragmentation and weak community oversight are named drivers of unreliable and inequitable service, but the legal and administrative mechanism is not tested; no effect estimate.
pdf_note: PhD dissertation, University of Alabama, 2026; about 144,000 characters read (abstract, Chapter 1 and parts of Chapters 2-3); the later chapters and appendices were only skimmed for governance and methods passages
notes: Governance fragmentation is a context finding, not a tested exposure.
